
## Getting useful information 

How else can we **effectively convey information?**

```r
unemp_df <- read_csv("data/unemployment.csv")
```

```{=typst}
#align(center)[
```

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE} 
#| label: empty-plot
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: 30%


read_csv('data/unemployment.csv') %>%
    group_by(Year) %>%
    summarise(avg_unemp = mean(Unrate)) %>% 
    tail(8) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
        Year='Year',
        avg_unemp='Average Unemployment'
    ) %>%
    fmt_number(
        columns=avg_unemp,
        n_sigfig=2
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
        style=cell_text(
            size='20pt'
            ),
        locations=list(
            cells_body(),
            cells_column_labels()
        )
    ) %>%
    opt_row_striping() 
    #knitr::kable(digits = 2, booktabs = TRUE, col.names = c("Year", #"Average Unemployment")) %>%
    #kable_styling(latex_options = "striped")
```
